metadata.note: The Ithaca-Auburn Short Line -- the last railroad built in Tompkins County, and a famously ill-conceived one. Promoted by Albert H. Flint and chartered March 16 1900 as the New York, Auburn and Lansing Railroad, it revived the old 'Murdock Line' grade (graded 1853-54, never operated) and the grade of the New York and Oswego Midland's Auburn Branch / Ithaca, Auburn and Western. Construction began in 1906 from the Auburn end and reached South Lansing March 1 1908; the line into Ithaca opened December 12 1908. The railroad was split by traction: about 29 miles of steam road ran Auburn - South Lansing (entering Auburn over Lehigh Valley track from Genoa Junction), while the ~7 miles from South Lansing down into Ithaca were strung with overhead wire and worked by streetcars leased from the Ithaca Street Railway (Ithaca Traction from 1912), using that company's Tioga Street line from downtown Ithaca to Percy Field. Passengers between Ithaca and Auburn changed cars at South Lansing. A 0.5-mile electrified branch to the Rogues' Harbor Inn at South Lansing opened in 1909 (not drawn; closed October 19 1920). The company went into receivership in 1912 -- the receiver kept running NYA&L trains -- and was reorganized in 1914 as the Central New York Southern Railroad, which bought McKeen gas-electric cars and rebuilt the bottom of the hill as an S-bend from Percy Field. The McKeens did NOT run through to downtown Ithaca: the city refused gas cars on Tioga Street, so the transfer moved from South Lansing to a waiting track at Percy Field. It never paid: the route crossed very thinly settled country and paralleled the improving state Route 34. The last run over the main line was in October 1923 (19th per Wikipedia, 31st per the Pomeroy marker), the ICC approved abandonment April 29 1924, and rail was lifted in 1925 -- except Percy Field - Remington, which Ithaca Traction kept to c.1931 as a freight track to the Remington power station (not drawn, Rule 1). Not to be confused with the earlier Ithaca, Auburn and Western Railroad (1876-1891), a different company over part of the same grade, whose Auburn end passed to the Lehigh Valley. GEOMETRY re-traced 2026-10-19 from OpenStreetMap, which maps most of the grade by name; see each feature's geometry_quality.

metadata.not_yet_sourced: No timetable for the road was seen, so every headway is an estimate. Open questions (research report research/branches/new_york_auburn_and_lansing_railroad.txt, UNRESOLVED): (1) the CNYS organization and conveyance days (28 May / 14 Jul 1914) are carried from older Wikipedia text and not re-verified -- the year is solid; (2) last run 19 vs 31 Oct 1923; (3) whether any passenger trains ran Auburn - Genoa in 1907 before the 1 Mar 1908 opening to South Lansing; (4) frequency: four trains a day vs six each way falling to two, and the CNYS 'more daily trips' of 1914; (5) who ran electric cars Ithaca - South Lansing after 1914, and until when through streetcars ran to South Lansing rather than McKeens only above Percy Field; (6) whether Asbury, Esty and McKinney in branchline table 213 were Short Line stops or merged Lehigh Valley names (OSM maps the Short Line grade past Esty Drive and McKinneys hamlet, which supports Short Line stops); (7) the Auburn terminal -- an own station on Monroe Street, or the LV station via the Genoa Junction - Auburn LV track -- and which way the line entered Auburn; (8) the 1908-1914 alignment at the bottom of the hill (via or near the Ithaca Street Railway's Cayuga Heights loop), not traced.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.interurban_audit: 2026-08-24: features on this layer that are inter-city electric railways were retagged mode='interurban' (previously 'streetcar' or 'intercity_rail') so the map can draw them distinctly from city streetcars and from steam roads. See CLAUDE.md Rule 7.
source_conflicts: Last main-line run: 19 Oct 1923 (Wikipedia) vs 31 Oct 1923 (Pomeroy marker). Same year; does not affect the drawn span. 19 Oct is also Wikipedia's date for the 1920 Rogues' Harbor closure, which suggests one of the two may be a copying error.
Frequency: four trains a day Ithaca - Auburn (Wikipedia) vs six trips a day each way, later two (ithaca.com).

Start of the CNYS era: 1914 (Wikipedia; Ithaca Journal 23 Jun 1914 via the Pomeroy marker) vs 1912 (vizettes.com). 1912 is the receivership, in which the receiver ran NYA&L trains; the split is drawn at 1914.
Opening: Genoa - Auburn 'finished in 1907' with a Genoa depot '1907-1924' (Pomeroy marker) vs opening to South Lansing 1 Mar 1908 (Wikipedia). No 1907 passenger operation found; drawn from 1908.

Route below South Lansing: Wikipedia says the line climbed 'through Renwick and Twin Glens, parallel to and below the current New York State Route 13'; OSM maps it on the east-shore hillside past Esty and McKinneys. The OSM mapping was followed.
metadata.freight_only_audit: 2026-10-19: removed the feature 'Ithaca Traction: Ithaca - Remington' (id ithaca-traction-ithaca-remington, drawn 1923-1931). Every source that says what the stub was for describes freight -- kept 'to serve a powerhouse until 1931' (Wikipedia), 'the freight track to the Remington power station' (Rossiter 2017, after Palmer 2011) -- and none describes a passenger car on it after Oct 1923 (Rule 1). It was also coloured in the NYA&L colour for a different company and its geometry ran ~3 mi past Remington. The street railway's own Tioga Street - Renwick Park cars (to Stewart Park, 1894-1935) are a different line and are not drawn anywhere in data/.
metadata.ownership_split_audit: 2026-10-19 (Rule 4): the steam and electric features previously ran 1908-1923 in the New York, Auburn and Lansing colour, with 1914-1923 segments that named the Central New York Southern. Each was split at the 1914 reorganization into two features sharing identical geometry: NYA&L 1908-1914 (ids ithaca-auburn-short-line-steam-nyal / -electric-nyal, colour unchanged) and Central New York Southern 1914-1923 (ids ithaca-auburn-short-line-steam-cnys / -electric-cnys, new colour #7AA621, used by no other company in data/). The 1912 receivership and the March 1923 foreclosure sale to Ford, Bacon & Davis are not splits: no new operator ran the trains.
metadata.not_drawn: Deliberately not drawn: (a) the 0.5 mi electric spur South Lansing - Rogues' Harbor Inn (1909-1920; NYA&L to 1914, CNYS after) -- too short to show at map scale; (b) the predecessor New York and Oswego Midland Auburn Branch worked by the Utica, Ithaca and Elmira (Freeville - Scipio Centre, one 1875 Official Guide anchor) and the Ithaca, Auburn and Western (Freeville - Auburn, 1876-1891, anchors 1881/1887 low confidence with an unresolved Auburn-extension date and guide-letter meaning) -- both are different companies over part of this grade and belong in their own layers once their dates are settled; the report recommends leaving them off; (c) the Ithaca - Remington freight stub (see freight_only_audit); (d) the 1853-54 Murdock grade, which never carried a train.
metadata.retrace: 2026-10-19: rebuilt from research/branches/new_york_auburn_and_lansing_railroad.txt. Geometry replaced: the previous 5-7-point straight-line waypoint lines (28.5 + 6.9 mi; the electric one ran due north from Percy Field and the steam one ran straight from Mapleton into central Auburn) were replaced by an OSM trace (29.6 + 7.2 mi vs 29.3 + 7.2 documented). Notes corrected: the McKeen cars did not end the transfer (it moved to Percy Field); the 1912 receivership is not an operator change; frequency conflict recorded.

segments.note: Steam section, about 29 miles Auburn - South Lansing via Genoa Junction (Lehigh Valley track into Auburn), Mapleton, Merrifield, Venice Center, Genoa and North Lansing. Opened to South Lansing 1 Mar 1908 (Wikipedia, citing Lee & Rossiter 2008); passengers for Ithaca changed to electric cars at South Lansing. The Pomeroy marker at Genoa says the Genoa - Auburn section was finished in 1907 and gives the Genoa depot as '1907-1924' -- construction and depot dates, not proof of 1907 passenger trains, so the drawn start stays 1908. The company went into receivership in 1912, but the receiver kept running New York, Auburn and Lansing trains, so 1912 is not an operator change; the segment ends at the 1914 reorganization as the Central New York Southern (Ithaca Journal 23 Jun 1914 via the Pomeroy marker). FREQUENCY CONFLICT: four trains a day (Wikipedia) vs 'six trips a day in each direction (later dwindling to two)' (ithaca.com 'Making Tracks'); headway 240 is an estimate either way.
sources: Segment-level: start year 1908 from Wikipedia (opening to South Lansing 1 Mar 1908, citing Lee & Rossiter 2008); end year 1914 = reorganization as Central New York Southern, Ithaca Journal 23 Jun 1914 as quoted on the Pomeroy Foundation marker, and Wikipedia. Headway NOT SOURCED: no timetable for the road was seen; the headway is an estimate.

segments.note: Electric section, about 7 miles South Lansing - Ithaca, opened into Ithaca 12 Dec 1908 (Wikipedia). Worked by the New York, Auburn and Lansing with streetcars LEASED from the Ithaca Street Railway (reorganized as Ithaca Traction in 1912, so the lessor from 1912 was Ithaca Traction) -- an NYA&L service, not a street-railway route. The first mile, State St to Percy Field, ran over the street railway's own Tioga Street line (electric from June 1892, per D.G. Rossiter's 2017 tour guide), terminating in the 100 block of N. Tioga St between State and Seneca. Power came from the Remington power plant (ithaca.com). A 0.5-mile electric spur to the Rogues' Harbor Inn opened in 1909 (not drawn). The 1912 receivership did not change the operator; the segment ends at the 1914 reorganization as the Central New York Southern. Headway 60 is an estimate; no schedule for the electric cars was found.

Headway NOT SOURCED: no timetable for the road was seen; the headway is an estimate.

segments.note: Central New York Southern Railroad, the reorganized successor of the New York, Auburn and Lansing (organized 28 May 1914, property conveyed 14 Jul 1914 per earlier Wikipedia text, not re-verified; the Ithaca Journal of 23 Jun 1914, quoted on the Pomeroy marker, reported the buyout with a new schedule of more daily trips and new cars). Two McKeen gas-electric cars (#101, #102 tentatively) were bought to speed the run, but they did NOT end the transfer: the City of Ithaca would not let gas cars on its streets, so from 1914 the McKeens ran Auburn - Percy Field and passengers changed to streetcars at a waiting track on the east side of Percy Field (Wikipedia; Rossiter tour guide stop 11) -- the transfer moved from South Lansing to Percy Field. The March 1923 foreclosure sale to Ford, Bacon & Davis was not an operator change; trains ran on under the CNYS name. LAST RUN CONFLICT: 19 Oct 1923 (Wikipedia) vs 31 Oct 1923 (Pomeroy marker); either way 1923 is the last passenger year. ICC abandonment decided 29 Apr 1924 (Finance Docket 2722) and rail lifted 1925 -- neither is a passenger year. Headway 240 is an estimate; the 1914 'more daily trips' is not quantified.

segments.note: Central New York Southern era on the electrified South Lansing - Ithaca section. From 1914 the lowest section was rebuilt as an S-bend from Percy Field (abutment over East Shore Drive survives), and the McKeen gas-electric cars ran through from Auburn as far as Percy Field, where passengers changed to streetcars for the run down N. Tioga Street -- the City of Ithaca barred the gas cars from its streets (Wikipedia; Rossiter tour guide stop 11). So passenger trains used this whole section 1914-1923, but WHO ran electric cars above Percy Field after 1914, and until when through streetcars still ran to South Lansing, is not established (Rossiter: the Tioga St terminus served 'streetcars to South Lansing and Rogue's Harbor'; the Rogues' Harbor spur, not drawn, closed 19 Oct 1920 per Wikipedia). Last run Oct 1923 (19 Oct per Wikipedia, 31 Oct per the Pomeroy marker). The Ithaca - Remington stub kept after 1923 was freight to the Remington power station and is not drawn. Headway 60 is an estimate.
